vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: vizclaw
Version: 1.0.3

The VizClaw skill is designed to stream OpenClaw events to the VizClaw visualization service. The `scripts/connect.py` file handles event parsing and sends them via WebSockets or HTTP POST to `api.vizclaw.com`, which is consistent with the skill's stated purpose. The `SKILL.md` file provides installation and usage instructions, including direct execution of the Python script from `vizclaw.com`, which is the expected source. The script includes features like redaction modes for sensitive data and does not exhibit any signs of unauthorized data exfiltration, malicious execution, persistence, or prompt injection with harmful intent.

llm.summary: This skill is purpose-aligned, but it tells users to run mutable remote code and streams detailed agent content to VizClaw by default, so it needs careful review before installation.

dimensions.detail: The skill can read user-selected stdin streams, local OpenClaw log files, local or remote OpenClaw websockets, and gateway event streams, then send mapped events to wss://api.vizclaw.com/ws/report or https://api.vizclaw.com/api/report. This is coherent for visualization but high-impact because agent logs may contain private code or secrets.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The install command uses npx clawhub@latest, and the script declares an unpinned websockets dependency. The artifact also ships a local script, but the documented remote uv run path bypasses a stable reviewed local copy.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md documents direct execution of a mutable remote Python script from vizclaw.com and a JSONL pipe into that remote script. The safety note mentions overview/hidden redaction and warns not to stream secrets, but it does not clearly scope the default detailed transmission or require explicit consent.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No system service, scheduled task, privilege escalation, or durable local persistence was found. The script does keep up to 400 non-heartbeat events in an in-memory replay buffer and places the OpenClaw gateway token into the gateway URL query string as well as an Authorization header.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is VizClaw visualization of OpenClaw runs, and the script's network reporting, JSONL/stdin, websocket, gateway, and log-tail inputs fit that purpose; however, detailed mode is the default and preserves prompt, response, task, report, tool, skill, reminder, and error text for remote transmission.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending OpenClaw run content to VizClaw. Prefer overview mode for normal use, avoid streaming secrets or private project data, do not run the remote uv URL unless you trust that live hosted script, and prefer pinned/reviewed local versions where available.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Network streaming and local input reading are expected for this bridge, but the artifact lacks clear permission scoping and does not fully explain what detailed mode sends off-host.
[RP1] unexpected: Use of clawhub@latest is not needed for the skill's purpose and creates a mutable supply-chain boundary, though no malicious package behavior was established from the inspected artifact.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Adding the OpenClaw gateway token to the websocket query string is not necessary when an Authorization header is also sent and can expose the token in logs or diagnostics.
[SQP-2] expected: Forwarding event content is central to VizClaw, but the default detailed mode and sparse warning make the sensitive-data implications under-disclosed.
[E1] expected: The external VizClaw API destination is expected for live-room visualization, but it is still sensitive because the default payloads can contain agent content.
[T03] unexpected: The documentation instructs users to execute Python directly from a mutable remote URL even though a local script is present, which makes the reviewed payload non-stable.
[T09] expected: The inspected code confirms detailed event text can be transmitted to external VizClaw endpoints by default; this is purpose-aligned but insufficiently minimized.
[T08] unexpected: Unpinned runtime and install dependencies are a supply-chain review gap, not evidence that the current dependencies are malicious.
